workflow: per-object image measurements exported as CSV, then analysed elsewhere
quote: According to our user survey, respondents mentioned that GraphPad Prism was the 2nd-most popular data analysis software used with CellProfiler data.
problem: Image-analysis output routinely leaves the image tool and is re-entered into a separate stats/graphing program
need: Import per-object CSV exports from image-analysis tools directly, with the header row becoming column titles

workflow: classifier-positive vs negative distributions as box plots
quote: I think that Prism has better box plots than R for graphing classifier rule +/- distributions. That is why I use it.
problem: Chooses the plotting tool for its default box-plot quality rather than for its analysis
need: Produce publication-quality box plots by default without scripting

workflow: foci per nucleus and nuclear/cytoplasmic intensity ratios per well
quote: How to analyse statistical significances? Is it required to learn R, Python etc., to make a proper plot?
problem: After generating the measurement spreadsheet the user does not know how to test significance or plot without learning to code
need: Take an image-analysis spreadsheet and guide the user from it to a test and a plot without code

workflow: plotting per-object measurements (one row per cell)
quote: Prism's stats functions are pretty good in my experience, but some of the older versions can struggle plotting very large numbers of points onto a graph.
problem: Per-cell data sets have very many points and the graphing tool slows down or struggles to plot them
need: Plot tens of thousands of per-cell points responsively

workflow: whole-slide detections: mean and SD of a nuclear feature per case, 150 cases
quote: But I have more than 150 cases which have around 1million data point per case. So when I tried to export the interesting features from detection measurement, it couldn't cope to transfer 150 cases at the same time with csv format.
problem: Exporting a million detections per case for 150 cases as CSV fails, so per-case summaries cannot be built
need: Accept very large per-object tables and summarise them per case (mean, SD) in batch

workflow: batch spot-detection results saved for spreadsheet analysis
quote: I noticed that all her xml files created or appended by Icy, to store the batch data from Spot Detector, but also for ROI information, are in the GraphPadPrism format, whereas mines are in Excel.
problem: Results file written in one program's XML format cannot be opened by a colleague's spreadsheet software
need: Read and write open, unambiguous formats (CSV/XLSX) and detect other tools' XML formats on import

workflow: autophagy figures per cell, 3 treated cultures each with a control, ~100 cells each
quote: Then I decided to pool all treated cells and all controls for a general comparison. The question, more specifically, is: do I have the right, statistically, to do so?
problem: Wants to pool ~600 cells from three independent repeats and treat each cell as n
need: Ask what the independent unit is (culture/repeat vs cell) and test on per-repeat summaries, showing cells as a SuperPlot

workflow: checking whether three experimental runs can be lumped
quote: Is there a statistical means to prove that this assumption is not wrong? I tried the CV. ... you are right, lumping runs is not a good idea.
problem: No easy way to check run-to-run (between-experiment) variance before lumping runs; tried comparing CVs
need: Include experiment/run as a factor (blocking or nested model) and show the run-to-run variance explicitly

workflow: 96-well plate, 3 wells x 9 images x ~40 cells per condition
quote: For each biological replicate I have several technical replicates. How do I calculate an error (or the SD for that matter) for the biological replicates that takes into account the errors of the replicates?
problem: Does not know how to compute error bars for biological replicates when each is built from technical replicates
need: Aggregate technical replicates to one value per biological replicate and explain which SD/SEM the error bar shows

workflow: EU incorporation per cell, 3 wells per drug treatment
quote: How can I estimate the minimum number of cells we should analyse per well?
problem: No way to decide how many cells per well to image/analyse
need: Estimate required cells per well (and wells per condition) from pilot variance

workflow: mean of three well means, each with its own uncertainty
quote: how do I calculate the SEM for the average reading of the three replicates (that is, SEM(x..)) bearing in mind that each of the well averages (xi.) also has an uncertainty.
problem: Unsure how within-well (cell) and between-well variance combine into the reported SEM
need: Compute summary statistics for nested data (cells within wells) and state which level the SEM refers to

workflow: nuclei per mm2 and % pH3-positive; 3 coverslips x 3 tilescans x 9 sub-tiles per condition
quote: It seems inappropriate to put the counts for each of my 9th of a tile. But should I just create an average value for each region? Or for each coverslip? My question is - at what point do you take the mean?
problem: Does not know at which level (sub-tile, tilescan, coverslip) to average before graphing
need: Ask for the hierarchy (field within coverslip within condition) and average up to the replicate level automatically

quote: Some people divide up subsections of images/coverslip to p-hack the results, but I suspect there are issues with that unless you are aware that there is reason for variation across the coverslip.
problem: Splitting images into sub-regions inflates n (pseudoreplication) and can manufacture significance
need: Warn when the number of data points exceeds the number of independent samples and test at the sample level

workflow: RNAscope in brain regions, 9 vs 9 animals, 3 probes
quote: Is the above calculation a good way to get out the num positive per channel and to eventually compare those values across our samples and conditions with an t-test/anova in R?
problem: Unsure whether a home-made normalised metric is valid and which test to use across conditions
need: Explain what a per-area/per-cell metric is normalised to and suggest the test for 9 vs 9 animals

quote: Unfortunately for whole brain slides we needed to image all the samples separately, therefore for the detection of the probes with qupath we set unbiased different thresholds for each sample.
problem: Different thresholds per sample may make counts incomparable between groups
need: Record per-sample analysis settings with the data and flag when groups were processed with different parameters

quote: What statistical test(s) should I run to see statistically significant differences in the Jaccard indices and F1 measures among the software tested? My data analysis software acumen is limited to Excel and JMP. I don't know how to use Jupyter notebooks.
problem: Needs to compare several methods on the same images but does not know which test and cannot code
need: Design-first chooser: same images measured by k methods means repeated-measures / Friedman, no coding

quote: Also consider Bland-Altman agreement analysis. ... It is also very easy to do, you can probably do it in a spreadsheet.
problem: Method comparison is being framed as significance testing instead of agreement
need: Offer Bland-Altman (and multi-method pairwise Bland-Altman) for method-comparison data

workflow: YAP IHC H-scores per field, disease vs control
quote: Is this method valid for reliably comparing total YAP expression (nuclear + cytoplasmic) and nuclear-specific YAP expression between groups?
problem: Unsure whether per-field H-scores from batch scripts are valid for a group comparison
need: State the unit of analysis (patient vs field) and the scale of the score before comparing groups

quote: You can't use optical density means, the values aren't really linear nor are they meaningful on a scale.
problem: Users average DAB OD values as if they were linear quantities
need: Warn when averaging non-linear units and suggest percentage positive instead

workflow: live-cell MFI, 3 wells per group x 5 FOV, 7 time points
quote: I am worried that the second method is pseudoreplication, but the first method feels like I am losing the nuance of the cell-to-cell variability.
problem: Torn between N=3 wells and N=15 FOVs (or thousands of cells) for a t-test
need: Test at the well level while still displaying every cell (SuperPlot), and explain why

workflow: lab practice for binning cells into data points
quote: However, I have seen others in my lab combine all cells from the 3 wells (total of 15 FOVs) and average them into smaller bins (e.g., every 100 cells = 1 data point) or treat every FOV as a separate data point.
problem: Lab members inflate n by binning cells or treating FOVs as replicates
need: Detect nested structure in the data table and refuse/flag tests that use sub-replicate units as n

workflow: intensity vs distance profiles in CA1
quote: The problem is, there is a brightness variability in some samples, even though we took them all under the same conditions.
problem: Line profiles from different images differ in baseline brightness so curves are not comparable
need: Normalise profiles to a reference region/baseline and rescale distance to a common axis before averaging

workflow: 6 markers x 3 conditions, mean grey value with uneven confluence
quote: The only method that showed the changes we would expect for each marker was with the DAPI MGV, but I am concerned that this method is not accurately taking into account the confluence issue we have had with these cells.
problem: Tried several normalisations and is tempted to keep the one that gives the expected result
need: Pre-specify the normalisation and show results under each candidate so the choice is transparent

quote: So how can their signal say anything meaningful about variability in *my sample*?
problem: Unclear what a normalisation reference actually corrects for (instrument vs sample variability)
need: Explain what each normalisation removes and what variance remains

quote: When I use the Cluster Cells function, select "Standardize: subtract Mean divide by STD" and normalize per dataset. How exactly the normalization is done?
problem: Does not know how the software standardised the data before clustering
need: Document exactly which standardisation is applied (per marker, per dataset, per sample)

workflow: GFP normalised to DAPI in fly brain max projections
quote: The problem is that I am trying to normalize the GFP to the Dapi, and I have not done this before.
problem: PI asks for normalisation to DAPI and the student does not know how to do it
need: Guided ratio normalisation (signal/reference channel) with area accounted for

quote: I have tried to subtract background, but that doesn't fix my actual problem of normalizing my pictures so I can compare them.
problem: Background differs between tissues so one threshold captures signal in one sample and nothing in another
need: Normalise background between images before thresholding and report the method

workflow: western blot normalisation to loading control
quote: Would you please clarify the principle behind each strategy and which one should I follow, as I tried both and got different values!!!
problem: Two normalisation orders (normalise loading control first vs divide then normalise) give different numbers
need: Implement one documented western-blot normalisation workflow (target/loading control, then relative to control lane)

workflow: nuclear protein intensity normalised to DAPI
quote: I have seen papers where they simply divide the intensity for the protein of interest with the nuclear intensity. Is there a good reference that shows that the nuclear and protein intensities co-varies linearly when the potentially confounding factors change?
problem: Ratio normalisation is used without checking that the two signals scale linearly
need: Plot signal vs reference before normalising and warn when the ratio assumption fails

workflow: particle tracking in neurons, reviewer response
quote: The reviewer asks for normalization of the particle channel to the cytoplasmic fill channel to show that the movement of particles is not caused by the changes in morphology. ... but I can't really say no to a reviewer and expect to have a paper published.
problem: A reviewer demands a normalisation the author does not know how to do sensibly
need: Offer standard channel-ratio normalisation with a methods text to cite in the response

workflow: Sholl profiles, control vs experimental group
quote: now that i have these 2 graphs how i insert them into one so i can make my comparisons.
problem: Group-mean curves end up in two separate plots and cannot be overlaid easily
need: Overlay several groups' mean curves with error bands on one XY graph

quote: Is it possible to conduct statistical analysis within SNT or do i have to transfer my data to another software?
problem: Statistics for comparing profiles are not available where the data was produced
need: Compare whole curves between groups (e.g. two-way ANOVA radius x group or curve comparison)

workflow: comparing area measurements of two scripts on the same images
quote: To compare these two scripts, I compare the area data result by using the t-test. So, I am wondering what hypothesis I can make?
problem: Uses an unpaired t-test to compare two measurement methods on the same objects
need: Recognise method-comparison designs and offer paired analysis plus Bland-Altman agreement

workflow: mean MSD curves for several drug conditions
quote: I used plotMeanMSD for multiple drug conditions on the same plot. All working great. However, can I do statistical tests for the different conditions? ... I had the same question
problem: Can plot mean curves per condition but has no way to test whether the curves differ
need: Statistical comparison of curves between conditions (fit parameters or curve-level test)

workflow: mitochondrial particles within cells within animals within treatment
quote: I'm wondering if there is a way that I can leverage the large number of measurements to increase the statistical power of my analysis. ... I'm considering using nested three-factor ANOVA.
problem: Many particle measurements nested in cells and animals; risk of treating particles as n
need: Nested/mixed model with animal as the unit, available without scripting

quote: How to export measurement data to Excel? I can't find any function that allows this.
problem: No direct export from the image tool to a spreadsheet
need: Accept CSV/TSV exports from image tools directly so no Excel step is needed

workflow: multiplex IF positive cells per DAPI vs per tissue area
quote: while this two approach statistic way should be same comparison result ,however using the positive cell number /DAPI can reached to more expected data
problem: Two normalisations answer different questions; user prefers the one giving the expected result
need: Explain what each denominator measures and keep the chosen one fixed before testing

workflow: Pearson/Manders coefficients, ~20 images WT vs mutant
quote: So, can I do simple averages on the coefficient values I got out of each image from the set? Or is there something I am missing? ... I do have same problem and have not found clear solution yet.
problem: Does not know how to summarise and compare per-image colocalisation coefficients
need: Guide from per-image coefficients to a per-sample summary and a two-group test

workflow: colocalisation in several slices per individual, two cohorts
quote: But then I don't know how to have an average "coefficient" for each individuals in order to plot the coefficients for each individuals and then do a t-test between the two groups to see a difference.
problem: Needs to aggregate several slices per individual before comparing cohorts
need: Aggregate measurements to one value per individual, plot individuals and test between groups

workflow: biofilm intensity-time curves, 10 repeats on different days
quote: Currently, the difficulty I have is how to scale these experiments (for the 10 days) inorder to get an average intensity-time data for all the repeats
problem: Cannot combine repeated time courses from different days into one mean curve
need: Average replicate time courses with per-repeat curves shown (time-series SuperPlot) and error bands

quote: There's also the ... corresponding online tool ... that you can use to plot your data if you are not proficient with coding to do it yourself.
problem: Users who cannot code are pointed to a separate web tool just to make a SuperPlot
need: Built-in SuperPlots (cells coloured by replicate, replicate means overlaid) without code

workflow: 3 biological x 3 technical replicates of biofilm z-stacks
quote: Is there a way to include a t-test (or sth similar) under method in the visualization? ... regarding the t-test, we currently don´t have anything like this implemented.
problem: Image tool has visualisation but no statistics; user must export to R/Python
need: Accept the exported replicate table and run the test with technical replicates aggregated

quote: However, the background for each slide is different, and we cannot use a unified threshold for all slides.
problem: Slide-to-slide background prevents a single positivity threshold
need: Per-slide normalisation against controls before applying a common threshold

quote: I have been thinking of setting a threshold based on a single control image and just normalizing the background of all images. Does this make sense, or are there potential inaccuracies or errors that can occur from this method?
problem: Unsure whether a background normalisation will bias the group comparison
need: Show the effect of the chosen background correction on the group comparison

quote: I'm not sure how to convert the .tif images to .gpr format, or how to statistically analyze the results I obtained from ImageJ.
problem: Stats packages need a format the user cannot produce; no path from ImageJ numbers to a test
need: Accept plain spot-intensity tables and provide normalisation plus testing for antibody arrays

quote: I can't seem to get CellProfiler not to split some of the bands into 2 separate objects.

quote: Can someone quickly tell me where to find easy instructions to performing densitometry on a Western blot? I find the instructions provided to be incomplete and confusing.

need: Step-by-step guided densitometry from image to normalised values

quote: Everything I have found in the web so far was mostly going a in the wrong direction leading to non-reliable measurements! ... So, even while often suggested, drawing boxes around a band is not the proper way!
problem: Online western blot tutorials teach unreliable quantification
need: Densitometry workflow that follows published standards (linear range, total-protein normalisation)

quote: I would not recommend using ImageJ's Gel Analysis functions for Western Blot quantification because it is not flexible enough and does not allow to follow literature standards in full.
problem: The common free tool cannot implement the recommended standards
need: Support calibration, linear-range checks and total-protein normalisation for blots

quote: In selecting a ROI to measure area, IntDen and RawInDen, am I to say IntDen=colour intensity per that selected area=density of fibres in that selected area?
problem: Unsure what the exported intensity columns mean physically
need: Explain imported measurement columns and their units before analysis

quote: My goal is to have one excel file, with all my annotations measurements of each .czi file in my project.
problem: Measurements end up per image and must be merged by hand or by script
need: Import and stack many per-image result files into one table with an image identifier

quote: Now my question is, can I calculate the correlation coefficient (Pearson's r) by using the intensities values obtained from the two channel? I'm trying Graphpad Prism as software for the correlation analysis
problem: Unsure whether Pearson correlation of line-profile values is valid
need: Correlation with a warning that adjacent profile points are not independent

workflow: testing a web tool for blot figures
quote: I felt the operation was very smooth, and slicker than Excel or Graphpad, which is a big plus. ... How is data stored and managed? Specifically, is it stored on a third party cloud-service or handled on your server?
problem: Scientists will ask where unpublished data goes before using a web tool
need: Process data locally in the browser and say so plainly

workflow: cell counts per mm2 for a bar graph
quote: But the exported data is not normalized in cells per mm2 area, right? How to normalize it in fact I want to plot the bar graph in cells per mm2?
problem: Needs a derived density column before graphing
need: Compute derived columns (count / area) during import

workflow: MitoTracker red/green ratio, 4 treatments x 3 wells
quote: Ultimately, I would like to output the data to a spreadsheet where I can perform any remaining calculations that are necessary (such as the ratios) and transfer the data into Graphpad/Prism for statistical analysis.
problem: Pipeline needs a spreadsheet step for ratios and then a manual transfer into a stats program
need: Compute ratios on import and carry the per-cell table straight into the analysis

workflow: per-cell intensity ratios, image within well within treatment
quote: This would allow me to calculate the averages at multiple levels (per image, per well/replicate, and per treatment group), while having a large number of individual data points to input into GraphPad/Prism for statistical analysis and to produce a graph.
problem: Needs hierarchical summaries (image, well, group) from a per-cell table
need: Read hierarchical per-object data and summarise at each level, testing at the replicate level

quote: I've been trying to get the heatmap function working as demonstrated in your example, but I've found it a bit challenging to navigate the documentation and configuration files—especially without a programming background.
problem: Analysis package requires config files and coding the user lacks
need: Point-and-click import of a region table and heatmap without configuration files

workflow: Cell Painting, 3 plate replicates, 2 cell types
quote: I'm wondering at what point would it be appropriate to combine measurements from the multiple replicates, i.e. by taking the median or mean.
problem: Unclear order of aggregation and normalisation across plate replicates
need: Explicit pipeline: aggregate per well, normalise per plate to controls, then combine replicates

quote: The MCID system would measure optical density and then convert the value to fmol/mg of receptor binding. ... The challenge I'm facing with image J is that it measures mean gray value.
problem: Replacement tool lacks standard-curve conversion from optical density to binding units
need: Fit a standard curve from calibration standards and interpolate unknowns into physical units

quote: I've always used MCID but my computer just died and I'm not sure I can get a new computer that will run the MCID program since it it relatively old.
problem: Lab analysis depends on obsolete software that will not run on new computers
need: Platform-independent tool that will keep running on new machines

quote: Is there actually way to export overlays (in particular scale bars) from Fiji/ImageJ to vector formats like EPS, PDF or SVG mentioned above.
problem: Overlays and scale bars do not export as vectors for figure assembly
need: Export figures as editable vector files with raster parts embedded losslessly

quote: Currently, many publication figures either suffer from JPEG artifacts, are too low in resolution or massively blurred due to interpolation.
problem: Published figures are degraded by lossy export and resampling
need: Lossless, non-interpolated export at journal resolution

quote: Is there a (easy) way in Fiji to also do the layout of those images into a combined figure? I am not sure this is needed, one could just copy and paste into some other software.
problem: Figure layout requires a separate program
need: Arrange several panels into one figure with consistent sizing and export

quote: However I would like to generate an additional visual scatter plot (cytofluorogram) to correlate the two co-localization channels ... That's a pity that Cellprofiler does not have this feature

need: Scatter/2D-histogram of paired values with correlation shown

workflow: quartiles of a set of values

need: State which quartile definition is used so values match other software

quote: Can I get the statistics values as an output of the Violin plot node? Do I have to use another node to calculate the statistics again?
problem: Statistics shown on hover in a plot cannot be exported
need: Every plotted summary (median, quartiles) available as a table

quote: I expected to obtain results on the fold change of each of the treated samples in relation to the control sample. Could you please help me to get the fold change for individual samples?
problem: Wants per-sample fold changes (to plot replicates) but the tool only gives group-level results
need: Give per-replicate fold changes relative to the control mean alongside the group estimate

workflow: time course, logFC per replicate for ANOVA and error bars
quote: Without individual sample logFCs I can't really do that statistics. ... I was able to calculate my error bar by > logFC/t and put that in my Prism table.
problem: Back-calculates a standard error from logFC/t by hand to get error bars into a graphing program
need: Export fold changes with their SE/CI ready for graphing, and per-replicate values for downstream ANOVA

quote: What tool can I use in Galaxy to check for variance between my replicates to know if I need to exclude anyone from my analysis?
problem: No obvious way to check replicate consistency before deciding to exclude one
need: Replicate-agreement view (spread per replicate, correlation) with an explicit, recorded outlier decision

problem: Unsure whether to treat re-sequencing runs as replicates
need: Ask which files are technical repeats and collapse them before testing

workflow: 6 samples x 2 technical replicates, WT vs KO
quote: While now I need to combine each replicates into one sample for analysis (i.e. 3WT 3KO). Could anyone help on this? (which join or combine function should I use?)
problem: Cannot find how to merge technical replicates into one sample
need: One-step 'collapse technical replicates' (sum or mean) keyed by sample ID

quote: Can I use these tool without replication? Cause patient sample, for one condition I only run 1 time. ... Punch line: not using replicates produces invalid results
problem: Has one sample per condition and expects a statistical test anyway
need: Refuse inferential tests with n=1 per group, explain why, and offer descriptive output only

workflow: miRNA control vs treatment without replicates
quote: I know, replicate dataset must require for genuine calculation, but I don't have the choice.
problem: No replicates, but needs a differential result anyway
need: Clear n=1 handling: descriptive fold change, labelled as exploratory

workflow: normalising counts for 30 samples of one group

problem: Normalisation is locked inside a two-group test workflow
need: Offer normalisation as a standalone step independent of any comparison

workflow: volcano plot with genes of interest

need: Label points from a pasted list of names, matched case-insensitively

quote: But some dots, even if they are significantly expressed stay unlabeled while some other dots which seem less significant are labeled.
problem: Automatic labels do not go to the most significant points
need: Label top-N by a stated criterion and show which criterion was used

workflow: volcano plot with p = 0 and NA values

need: Cap -log10(p) at the floating-point floor with a marker, and report how many NA rows were omitted

workflow: volcano plot with points at the top

quote: I tried to adjust the" Minimum and maximum value for x axis", but the plot didn't change as my seeing
problem: Axis range setting silently has no effect unless both limits are filled
need: Axis limits that apply immediately and validate partial input

workflow: scatter plot with log Y axis
quote: I do not want to transform my entire data into log2(value) or log10(value) because I get errors when I do. I just want my Y axis to be in logarithmic scale, like in excel.
problem: Wants a log axis without transforming the data
need: Log-scale axis option separate from data transformation

quote: It's very difficult when trying to use them for a manuscript etc if the only output is a pdf that you need to screenshot.
problem: Plots only available as PDF; users screenshot them for figures
need: Export SVG, TIFF/PNG at chosen DPI and PDF

workflow: reference gene choice for qPCR in leukemic vs stem cells

quote: What type of information is represented on each axis of the MA plot? also what do the dots and the colors of the dots represent?
